clue.text: One can have a close shave with this murderer

definitions.text: One can have a close shave with this
definitions.meaning: an open razor with a long blade, the old barber's kind
a killer who slits victims' necks, or any violent ruffian

explanation.definitionFit: The open razor and the ruthless killer share one name, from slitting a neck.

clue.text: Conservative too old to get press attention

parts.note: overage means beyond the permitted age

explanation.surface: A Tory considered past it attracts the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting a story receives in newspapers and broadcasts.

clue.text: Military coat necessary to fight unicorn

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Armour needed for battling a mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket worn as part of a uniform.

clue.text: Nourishing treat most of the rich finish off

parts.note: to treat an illness is to heal it

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped
finish off means the end letter is removed

parts.note: rich means full, as in a full flavour

explanation.surface: A tasty snack: eating up most of a rich dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH, and 'finish off' cuts FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthful means wholesome, good for the body.

clue.text: Caruso left confused about kissing

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The tenor Caruso was bewildered on the subject of kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges CARUSO plus L. Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscular is an adjective meaning relating to the mouth or to kissing.

clue.text: Destroyer at sea using electric ray

definitions.meaning: a self-propelled underwater missile that sinks ships
a fish that stuns prey with an electric shock

explanation.definitionFit: The underwater missile was named after the numbing fish, so both senses share one word.

clue.text: Money for some of the players

definitions.meaning: an informal word for cash, chiefly in northern England
the trumpets, trombones and horns of an orchestra

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cash and also the metal-wind section of a band.

clue.text: Tea in raffish place, having left motorway

indicators.note: having left means these letters depart from the word

parts.note: Bohemia is the land of unconventional, raffish artists
M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Having a cuppa in a seedy spot after turning off the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: BOHEMIA, the home of bohemians, loses MI (the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway).
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, once the finest kind.

clue.text: Take pride in changing gear on car

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling smug about shifting gear in one's motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is overbearing self-importance, an excess of self-regard.

clue.text: Miss Australia?

parts.note: not a beauty queen but any young woman Down Under, in local slang

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like the beauty title; it is the Australian slang word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang this is a word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Chekhov's pawnbroker?

parts.note: a pawnbroker is slangily called 'uncle', so Chekhov's play about an uncle names one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so the title character of Chekhov's play Uncle Vanya becomes one through the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of a Chekhov play is an uncle, the slang term for one who lends against pledges.

clue.text: Boxer, say, pulling punch?

parts.note: Boxer is the loyal draught animal in Orwell's Animal Farm; a Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught animal

explanation.walkthrough: Boxer looks like a fighter pulling a punch; he is the heavy workhorse in Orwell's Animal Farm, and a Punch (Suffolk Punch) is a breed of such horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer in Animal Farm is a heavy draught animal, the kind that hauls wagons.

clue.text: Account given in novel clear about it

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next word
novel means new, so the following word is made anew in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A report delivered in a book that is clear about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' sounds like money but means a narration; 'novel' is the anagram signal, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed telling or narration of events.

clue.text: Len gave order for one of the leading new hooks

definitions.text: one of the leading new hooks

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of the two words are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Len issues instructions about some new hooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges LEN GAVE. 'hooks' as printed must be read as 'books': the Gospels lead the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangel is a gospel, and the Gospels lead off the New Testament.

clue.text: Idle fellow for whom virtue is its own reward?

definitions.text: for whom virtue is its own reward?
definitions.meaning: someone who behaves well and expects no payment at all

explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is called worthless; read literally, the phrase is someone virtuous with no payment.

clue.text: Old sweep, with inside information, is one for a flutter

parts.note: a sweep or extent is a range
a tip is a piece of inside knowledge

explanation.surface: An elderly chimney sweep with a racing tip is ready to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests a small bet, but here it is wings: the orange-tip is a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a European butterfly, an insect that flutters.

clue.text: Doubt could be confusing in the case

indicators.note: could be confusing means the letters may be muddled into another order

explanation.surface: Uncertainty might cloud the matter in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be confusing' rearranges IN THE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is indecision, a reluctance from uncertainty.

clue.text: Some relief work may be included in these figures

definitions.text: Some relief work may be included in these figures

parts.words: Some relief work may be included in these figures
parts.note: relief here is sculpture raised from a flat background, and figures are carved forms, not charity work or numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'relief work' and 'figures' suggest aid statistics; they are sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is sculpture collectively, which can include carvings in relief.

clue.text: Make surprisingly good landing after trip

definitions.text: Make surprisingly good landing after trip

parts.words: Make surprisingly good landing after trip
parts.note: literally, stumbling and still coming down upright, like a cat; figuratively, emerging lucky from a setback

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to come out of difficulty well, but read literally it is a stumble ending upright.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes escaping a mishap luckily, pictured as stumbling yet coming down upright.

clue.text: Sisters at entrance to nave remove head-dress

indicators.note: entrance to means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: to unhood is to take off a hood

explanation.surface: Nuns at the church door take off their veils.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunhood is the state of nuns, or nuns as a body, a sisterhood.

clue.text: Meant to avoid accident? On the contrary, partners have a child

indicators.note: on the contrary turns the small word before it the other way

parts.note: N and S, North and South, are partners at bridge
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Lovers produce a baby by accident, despite trying to avoid one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the contrary' turns ON into NO. North and South are partners at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-skid surface or tyre is designed to stop slipping and crashes.

clue.text: Soldiers holding strike in Macbeth's land

indicators.note: holding means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
to lam is to beat or strike

explanation.surface: Troops on industrial action in Shakespeare's Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis, a place in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth held the title Thane of Glamis, his Scottish territory.

clue.text: Fowl — a hooter on the lake, say

annotationWithheld.why: Fowl - a hooter on the lake, say (7): LEG (on) + HORN (hooter) is plausible but 'the lake, say' has no role in any parse found; scan matches the text
annotationWithheld.clue: Fowl — a hooter on the lake, say

clue.text: The gilt-edged alternative

indicators.note: edged means bordered, so the letters go on either side

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Safe government bonds as another investment choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gilt-edged' looks like safe government bonds; 'gilt' is gold in heraldry, and 'edged' places it on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different or alternative, the remaining option.

clue.text: Observation permitted in informal letter

parts.note: an observation is a remark or note
permitted means allowed, let

explanation.surface: A remark allowed into a casual letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for a short, casual message.

clue.text: Where airways go, one can get exotic apparel

parts.note: the bronchial airways lead into the lung
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Air routes lead to a place selling foreign clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airways' suggests airlines; they are breathing passages.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.

clue.text: Shotgun wedding embrace

parts.note: a wedding is a marriage, a match
an embrace is a hold, a lock (as in a lock of arms)

explanation.surface: A forced marriage, the bride and groom hugging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shotgun wedding' reads as a forced marriage, but 'Shotgun' alone is the definition, loosely used for an old firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early firearm fired by a slow-burning cord, here loosely called a gun for shooting.

clue.text: Grandma putting new heart into children's nurse

indicators.note: heart into means the letter goes into the middle of the next word

parts.note: a nana (nanny) is a children's nurse

explanation.surface: Granny gives the nanny some fresh courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is a familiar name for a grandmother.

clue.text: Exceptionally good purse distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine handbag's contents shared out among people.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal word for excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Special delivery held back in dangerous frontier town

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: dodgy is informal for risky or dangerous

indicators.note: held back means the word is put backwards

parts.note: a tice is an old cricket term for a yorker, a special kind of ball bowled

explanation.surface: Express post delayed in a risky Wild West settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' turns TICE (an old cricket word for a yorker) into ECIT, placed 'in' DODGY. Dodge City, Kansas, was a notorious Wild West town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge City in Kansas was a famous lawless settlement of the American West.
